intro: If you've been thinking about converting a tired bathroom into a sleek, accessible wet room, you're not alone — it's one of the most popular home improvements we see in Borthwickmill right now. Whether you're planning ahead for accessibility needs, updating a dated bathroom in a period cottage, or simply want a bathroom that looks and functions better, a professionally installed wet room makes a real difference to daily life. Done properly, it adds value to your home and lasts for decades. Done badly, it causes expensive water damage to floors and walls. This guide covers everything Borthwickmill homeowners need to know before taking the plunge.
localContext: Borthwickmill sits in Midlothian and its housing stock presents some interesting challenges for wet room installation. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up a good portion of homes here often have solid floors, irregular wall surfaces, and limited existing drainage routes — all of which need careful assessment before any work begins. Stone walls, in particular, require thorough tanking and waterproofing rather than the faster approaches that work fine in newer builds. The modern estates in and around Borthwickmill are generally more straightforward to work with, though cavity walls and timber floors still need proper preparation. It's also worth noting that Borthwickmill sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale can gradually affect shower heads, screens, and drainage channels over time. Specifying appropriate fittings and using a water softener or scale-inhibiting shower head is sensible advice for any installation here.
serviceDetail:
A proper wet room installation in Borthwickmill follows a clear sequence, and understanding it helps you plan realistically. The process begins with a site survey — a qualified installer will assess your existing bathroom, check floor and wall construction, and identify where drainage can realistically be positioned. This matters enormously in older Borthwickmill properties where you can't simply assume a drain can go anywhere you'd like.

Once the design is agreed, the first physical stage is stripping out the existing bathroom completely and preparing the subfloor. For a ground-floor room in a stone cottage, this often means working with a solid concrete base, which may need a screed applied to create the correct fall towards the drain. Timber floors in upper rooms require additional board reinforcement before tanking begins.

Tanking — applying a fully waterproof membrane across the floor and walls — is arguably the most critical stage. This is where shortcuts cause future misery. A reputable installer will apply multiple layers and pay particular attention to corners, pipe penetrations, and floor-to-wall junctions. After tanking, tiles or slip-rated flooring are laid, drainage channels fitted, and the shower fixtures installed. Plumbing connections are made, the heating is considered (underfloor heating is a popular addition in Borthwickmill wet rooms), and the room is fully sealed and grouted before a final check. From start to finish, expect around five to eight working days for a standard installation.
pricing: Wet room installation in Borthwickmill typically costs between £6,500 and £12,000, depending on the size of the room, the complexity of the existing structure, and the specification of finishes you choose. Older stone-built properties and period cottages tend to sit at the higher end because of additional preparation work — solid floor screeding, thicker tanking systems, and sometimes rerouting drainage. Modern estate homes with suspended timber floors are usually mid-range. High-end tiles, designer drainage channels, underfloor heating, and bespoke glass screens all push costs upward. A straightforward conversion in a modern property with mid-range finishes is realistically achievable around £6,500–£8,000, while a full premium specification in a character cottage is more likely £10,000–£12,000.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickmill and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for this kind of work. Local installers understand the construction quirks common to the area's stone cottages and older properties — they've dealt with awkward floor depths, irregular wall plaster, and drainage routes that don't follow the textbook. They're also easier to hold accountable if any snagging issues arise after completion, and they're more likely to have established relationships with local suppliers, which can help with materials availability and lead times. For a premium project costing upwards of six thousand pounds, working with someone who knows the local building stock is a worthwhile advantage.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone cottage in Borthwickmill?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than a modern build. Solid floors need screeding to create the right drainage fall, and stone walls need thorough tanking before any tiles go on. A good installer will survey the room properly first and flag any structural considerations before committing to a design. It's very achievable; it just needs the right approach from the start.

faqs.q: How long does wet room installation take in Borthwickmill?
faqs.a: Most installations take between five and eight working days, though complex older properties — particularly stone-built cottages with solid floors or tricky drainage routes — can take slightly longer. Your installer should give you a realistic timeline after the initial survey. It's worth planning for the bathroom to be out of use for the full duration, so a second WC or shower elsewhere in the house is helpful.

faqs.q: Will hard water in Borthwickmill cause problems with my new wet room?
faqs.a: Moderately hard water can cause limescale to build up on shower heads, screens, and drainage channels over time, but it won't affect the waterproofing or structure of the wet room itself. Specifying a quality shower head with an anti-scale function, using a squeegee regularly on screens, and occasionally descaling fittings is all you really need. Some homeowners in Borthwickmill also opt for an inline scale inhibitor on the water supply.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a Borthwickmill home?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly when it's well designed and professionally installed. A high-quality wet room is seen as a premium feature by buyers, and in Borthwickmill's mix of period cottages and modern properties, a beautifully finished bathroom stands out. Accessibility is also increasingly valued, meaning a level-access wet room appeals to a wide range of potential buyers. Poor installation, on the other hand, can be a red flag for surveyors, so quality of workmanship matters.
